question.text: What does 'closing a position' mean in the futures market?

answer.text: Executing an opposite transaction to reduce or eliminate an existing open position
Stopping all trading activity for the day
Transferring the position to another trader

explanation.text: The Logic: Closing a position means selling a contract that was previously bought, or buying a contract that was previously sold — an opposite transaction that reduces the open position. Squaring up before the close on the last trading day is the same concept applied to a futures contract approaching expiry. The Trap: Closing does not mean holding the contract to expiry — it is the act of actively offsetting the position with an opposite trade. Note: Squaring up is the term used for an offsetting buy/sell that flattens an open position before the last trading day's close.
